programme.subtitle: Build, inspect, refactor, and safely remove a small AWS network with Terraform.
programme.description: Start with no lab infrastructure and no assumed terminal knowledge. Learn how to open CloudShell or PowerShell, create and enter a folder, create and save Terraform files, understand each configuration block, initialise and validate Terraform, review and apply a saved plan, inspect AWS resources and state, refactor safely into a module, and remove everything in the correct order.
programme.learningOutcome: Confidently use a terminal and the complete beginner Terraform workflow while explaining why configuration, providers, plans, state, modules, verification, and cleanup matter.

tasks.title: Verify the AWS account and prepare Terraform
tasks.goal: Verify the correct training account and Region, confirm AWS CLI access, install Terraform, and create one clean working folder.
tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform can create or delete several connected resources in one operation. Confirming the account, Region, terminal, and folder first prevents changes in the wrong place and makes every later command predictable.

consoleSteps.title: Choose and open a terminal
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose one route for the whole lab: AWS CloudShell in your browser or Windows PowerShell on your computer.

instructions.text: Choose one route for the whole lab: AWS CloudShell in your browser or Windows PowerShell on your computer.
For CloudShell: sign in to the AWS Management Console, confirm this is your training account, and do not use the root user.
In the AWS Console top search box, type CloudShell and choose CloudShell from the results.
Wait until the CloudShell terminal shows a prompt ending with a dollar sign. This means it is ready for commands.
For PowerShell instead: open the Windows Start menu, type PowerShell, and choose Windows PowerShell.
Do not open both routes for the same run. Files created in CloudShell are not automatically the same files as those on your computer.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: One terminal is open and ready, and the learner knows where its files will be stored.

consoleSteps.title: Verify the AWS account and Region
consoleSteps.instruction: Run aws sts get-caller-identity. A command is run by typing it at the prompt and pressing Enter.

instructions.text: Run aws sts get-caller-identity. A command is run by typing it at the prompt and pressing Enter.
Find Account in the result and record the 12-digit value as [ACCOUNT_ID].
Find Arn and confirm it belongs to the authorised training user or role you intended to use.
In the AWS Console Region selector, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Run aws configure get region. If CloudShell returns no value, use the Console Region you just selected and include eu-west-2 in AWS commands.
Stop if the account ID or identity is not the expected training account. Do not continue in a production or unfamiliar account.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner has confirmed the exact AWS account, authorised identity, and eu-west-2 Region.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not continue when the account or identity is unexpected.

consoleSteps.title: Verify Terraform and create the working folder
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform version. If the command is not recognised, install Terraform using the linked official HashiCorp instructions, then close and reopen the terminal.

instructions.text: Run terraform version. If the command is not recognised, install Terraform using the linked official HashiCorp instructions, then close and reopen the terminal.
Record the displayed Terraform version. The required_version rule later prevents an incompatible version from being used accidentally.
CloudShell route: run mkdir -p ~/fa-terraform-beginner. mkdir means make directory; -p safely allows the folder to already exist.
CloudShell route: run cd ~/fa-terraform-beginner. cd means change directory.
CloudShell route: run pwd. Confirm the path ends with /fa-terraform-beginner.
PowerShell route: run New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-beginner" -Force. This creates the folder inside your Windows user folder.
PowerShell route: run Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-beginner". Set-Location enters that folder.
PowerShell route: run Get-Location. Confirm the path ends with fa-terraform-beginner.
Run ls -la in CloudShell or Get-ChildItem in PowerShell. The new folder should not contain unrelated files, credentials, or old Terraform state.

jsonBlocks.title: Terraform beginner command cheat sheet
jsonBlocks.content:
# Terraform Beginner Command Cheat Sheet

Use only the command section that matches your terminal. Run one command at a time.

## AWS CloudShell folder commands

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Show the current folder | `pwd` |
| List files and folders | `ls -la` |
| Create the lab folder | `mkdir -p ~/fa-terraform-beginner` |
| Enter the lab folder | `cd ~/fa-terraform-beginner` |
| Create or edit a file | `nano main.tf` |
| Save in nano | Press `Ctrl+O`, then `Enter` |
| Exit nano | Press `Ctrl+X` |
| Return to the parent folder | `cd ..` |

## Windows PowerShell folder commands

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Show the current folder | `Get-Location` |
| List files and folders | `Get-ChildItem` |
| Create the lab folder | `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-beginner" -Force` |
| Enter the lab folder | `Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-beginner"` |
| Create or edit a file | `notepad main.tf` |
| Return to the parent folder | `Set-Location ..` |

## AWS identity commands

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Show the signed-in AWS identity and account | `aws sts get-caller-identity` |
| Show the configured default Region | `aws configure get region` |
| Show the AWS CLI version | `aws --version` |

## Core Terraform commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `terraform version` | Shows the installed Terraform version. |
| `terraform fmt` | Reformats Terraform files consistently. |
| `terraform init` | Prepares the folder and downloads required providers. |
| `terraform validate` | Checks that the configuration is structurally valid. |
| `terraform plan -out=tfplan` | Calculates proposed changes and saves the reviewed plan. |
| `terraform show tfplan` | Displays the saved plan again. |
| `terraform apply tfplan` | Applies exactly the saved plan. |
| `terraform output` | Displays declared output values. |
| `terraform state list` | Lists resource addresses tracked in state. |
| `terraform plan` | Checks whether configuration and infrastructure still agree. |
| `terraform plan -destroy -out=destroy.tfplan` | Creates a saved teardown plan for review. |
| `terraform apply destroy.tfplan` | Applies exactly the reviewed teardown plan. |

## Common plan symbols

- `+ create` means Terraform proposes creating a resource.
- `~ update in-place` means Terraform proposes changing an existing resource without replacing it.
- `-/+ replace` means Terraform proposes destroying and recreating a resource. Stop and understand why.
- `- destroy` means Terraform proposes deleting a resource. Verify the exact address before continuing.
- `Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy` means no infrastructure change is required.

## Safety reminders

1. Confirm the AWS account and Region before every plan or apply.
2. Read every plan before applying it.
3. Never paste passwords, access keys, session tokens, or state content into files or chat.
4. Never delete a folder until Terraform-managed cloud resources have been removed and verified.

tasks.title: Write the first Terraform configuration
tasks.feature: Terraform providers, resources, variables, and outputs
tasks.goal: Create readable Terraform files for one VPC, one subnet, and one no-ingress security group.
tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform reads all .tf files in the working folder as one configuration. Separating provider settings, resources, variables, and outputs makes the configuration easier to understand, check, and reuse.

consoleSteps.title: Create main.tf
consoleSteps.instruction: Confirm the terminal is still inside fa-terraform-beginner by running pwd in CloudShell or Get-Location in PowerShell.

instructions.text: Confirm the terminal is still inside fa-terraform-beginner by running pwd in CloudShell or Get-Location in PowerShell.
CloudShell: run nano main.tf. Nano is a simple text editor inside the terminal.
PowerShell: run notepad main.tf. If Notepad asks whether to create the file, choose Yes.
Copy the complete supplied main.tf block and paste it into the empty editor. Do not paste the heading or Markdown marks.
CloudShell nano: press Ctrl+O, press Enter to confirm main.tf, then press Ctrl+X to exit.
PowerShell Notepad: choose File, Save, confirm the name is main.tf and not main.tf.txt, then close Notepad.
Understand the terraform block: it sets compatible Terraform and AWS provider versions.
Understand the provider block: it tells the AWS provider to work in eu-west-2 through the variable supplied in variables.tf.
Understand the resource blocks: they declare one VPC, one subnet inside that VPC, and one security group with no inbound rules.
The names start with fa-tf-beginner so they are easy to identify and remove. ManagedBy = Terraform shows which tool owns them.

consoleSteps.title: Create variables.tf and outputs.tf
consoleSteps.instruction: Create variables.tf with nano variables.tf in CloudShell or notepad variables.tf in PowerShell.

instructions.text: Create variables.tf with nano variables.tf in CloudShell or notepad variables.tf in PowerShell.
Paste the complete variables.tf block, then save and close the editor using the same method as main.tf.
The aws_region variable keeps the Region in one reusable place and defaults to eu-west-2.
Create outputs.tf with nano outputs.tf in CloudShell or notepad outputs.tf in PowerShell.
Paste the complete outputs.tf block, then save and close the editor.
Outputs give friendly names to the IDs Terraform receives from AWS after creation.
Run ls -la in CloudShell or Get-ChildItem in PowerShell and confirm main.tf, variables.tf, and outputs.tf are all listed.
If Windows shows main.tf.txt, rename it to main.tf before continuing. Terraform reads files ending in .tf.

consoleSteps.title: Format and validate the configuration
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform fmt. This applies Terraform’s standard spacing and layout; it does not create AWS resources.

instructions.text: Run terraform fmt. This applies Terraform’s standard spacing and layout; it does not create AWS resources.
Run terraform init. Terraform creates a hidden .terraform folder, downloads the AWS provider, and creates .terraform.lock.hcl.
Keep .terraform.lock.hcl because it records the selected provider version and checksums.
Run terraform validate. This checks whether the combined configuration is structurally valid.
Do not continue until validate reports Success! The configuration is valid.
If an error names a file and line number, reopen that file, compare it with the supplied block, save it, and run terraform fmt and terraform validate again.

tasks.title: Plan, apply, and inspect the Terraform resources
tasks.feature: Terraform init, validate, plan, apply, and state
tasks.goal: Review a saved plan, apply it once, and inspect the resulting AWS resources and Terraform state.
tasks.whyItMatters: The plan is Terraform’s safety preview. Saving and reviewing it before apply separates deciding what should change from making the actual AWS change.

consoleSteps.title: Create and understand the plan
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform plan -out=tfplan. The -out option saves the exact proposal in a binary plan file named tfplan.

instructions.text: Run terraform plan -out=tfplan. The -out option saves the exact proposal in a binary plan file named tfplan.
Read the summary and confirm Plan: 3 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
Find aws_vpc.lab, aws_subnet.lab, and aws_security_group.lab in the plan.
A plus sign means create. Stop if the plan shows destroy, replacement, a different Region, or resources outside this lab.
Run terraform show tfplan to display the saved plan again. This does not contact AWS or change infrastructure.
Confirm the CIDRs are 10.40.0.0/16 and 10.40.1.0/24 and all Name tags begin fa-tf-beginner.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The saved plan proposes exactly three new beginner resources and no deletion.
consoleSteps.warning: Never apply a plan you have not read.

consoleSteps.title: Apply the reviewed plan
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform apply tfplan. Supplying tfplan applies exactly the saved proposal you reviewed.

instructions.text: Run terraform apply tfplan. Supplying tfplan applies exactly the saved proposal you reviewed.
Wait for Apply complete! Resources: 3 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
Run terraform output and record vpc_id as [TF_VPC_ID], subnet_id as [TF_SUBNET_ID], and security_group_id as [TF_SG_ID].
Run terraform state list. State addresses are Terraform’s internal names for the real AWS objects.
Confirm the list contains aws_vpc.lab, aws_subnet.lab, and aws_security_group.lab.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Terraform creates three resources and records their addresses and AWS IDs in state.

consoleSteps.title: Verify the resources in AWS
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC and open VPC.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC and open VPC.
Choose Your VPCs in the left menu, search for fa-tf-beginner-vpc, and confirm its VPC ID equals [TF_VPC_ID].
Choose Subnets, search for fa-tf-beginner-subnet, and confirm its subnet ID equals [TF_SUBNET_ID] and its VPC equals [TF_VPC_ID].
Choose Security groups, search for fa-tf-beginner-sg, and confirm its group ID equals [TF_SG_ID].
Confirm the security group has no inbound rules. The lab does not need inbound network access.
Do not edit the resources in the Console. Terraform configuration is the intended source of truth.
Return to the terminal and run terraform plan without -out.
Confirm Terraform reports No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.

tasks.title: Refactor the VPC into a reusable module
tasks.feature: Terraform local modules, variables, outputs, and moved blocks
tasks.goal: Create a small local VPC module and preview a refactor without replacing the live VPC.
tasks.whyItMatters: Modules package related configuration behind clear inputs and outputs. The moved block tells Terraform that the existing VPC changed address in configuration, preventing an unnecessary destroy-and-recreate operation.

consoleSteps.title: Create the module folder and module file
consoleSteps.instruction: CloudShell: run mkdir -p modules/vpc. PowerShell: run New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "modules\vpc" -Force.

instructions.text: CloudShell: run mkdir -p modules/vpc. PowerShell: run New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "modules\vpc" -Force.
Create modules/vpc/main.tf with nano modules/vpc/main.tf in CloudShell or notepad modules\vpc\main.tf in PowerShell.
Paste the complete supplied modules/vpc/main.tf block and save the file.
The module declares name and cidr inputs, creates one VPC, and returns the VPC ID as output id.
The word this is the VPC resource name inside the module; its full new address becomes module.vpc.aws_vpc.this.

jsonBlocks.title: modules/vpc/main.tf

consoleSteps.expectedResult: modules/vpc/main.tf exists and contains a reusable VPC module.

consoleSteps.title: Replace the root configuration safely
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the root main.tf and replace its complete content with the supplied refactored main.tf block.

instructions.text: Open the root main.tf and replace its complete content with the supplied refactored main.tf block.
The module vpc block calls the local module and supplies the same name and CIDR as the existing VPC.
The moved block maps the old address aws_vpc.lab to module.vpc.aws_vpc.this.
The subnet and security group now use module.vpc.id so their VPC relationship remains intact.
Replace outputs.tf with the supplied refactored outputs.tf block so vpc_id uses module.vpc.id.
Save both files, then run terraform fmt -recursive and terraform validate.

consoleSteps.title: Prove the VPC will not be replaced

Run terraform plan -out=module-refactor.tfplan.

Run terraform state list and confirm module.vpc.aws_vpc.this replaces aws_vpc.lab while the subnet and security-group addresses remain.
Run terraform output and confirm vpc_id is still [TF_VPC_ID].

tasks.title: Destroy and verify the beginner lab
tasks.goal: Preview destruction, delete only the Terraform-managed beginner resources, and verify the account is clean.
tasks.whyItMatters: Terraform should remove the resources it owns while its configuration and state still exist. Deleting local files first would remove the information Terraform needs for a safe, reviewable teardown.

consoleSteps.title: Create and review the destroy plan
consoleSteps.instruction: Confirm the terminal is inside fa-terraform-beginner and run terraform state list.

instructions.text: Confirm the terminal is inside fa-terraform-beginner and run terraform state list.
Confirm state lists module.vpc.aws_vpc.this, aws_subnet.lab, and aws_security_group.lab.
Run terraform plan -destroy -out=destroy.tfplan.
Read every address and confirm exactly three resources are marked for destruction.
Confirm the names or IDs match [TF_VPC_ID], [TF_SUBNET_ID], and [TF_SG_ID].
Stop if any unrelated resource is listed. Do not continue merely because Terraform produced a plan.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The saved destroy plan removes only the three resources created by this lab.
consoleSteps.warning: Destruction is permanent. Verify all names, addresses, IDs, account, and Region.

consoleSteps.title: Apply the destroy plan and verify AWS
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform apply destroy.tfplan to apply exactly the reviewed teardown.

instructions.text: Run terraform apply destroy.tfplan to apply exactly the reviewed teardown.
Wait for Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 3 destroyed.
Run terraform state list. It should return directly to the prompt with no resource addresses.
In VPC, choose Your VPCs and confirm fa-tf-beginner-vpc and [TF_VPC_ID] are absent.
Choose Subnets and confirm fa-tf-beginner-subnet and [TF_SUBNET_ID] are absent.
Choose Security groups and confirm fa-tf-beginner-sg and [TF_SG_ID] are absent.
Confirm unrelated VPCs, subnets, and security groups are still present and unchanged.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Terraform state is empty and all three exact AWS resources are absent.

PowerShell: run Remove-Item -LiteralPath "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-beginner" -Recurse only after confirming the exact path.
Run ls -la in CloudShell or Get-ChildItem in PowerShell and confirm the exact lab folder is absent.
Record the final cleanup acknowledgement: cloud resources, Terraform state addresses, saved plans, and the local lab folder are removed.

warnings.safety: Create and delete only the exact fa-tf-beginner names and review every Terraform plan before applying it.
warnings.credentials: Use an authorised temporary training session. Never place passwords, access keys, session tokens, or Terraform state in Author, source control, screenshots, or chat.
warnings.region: Use eu-west-2 for every regional resource and verify the account before applying or destroying infrastructure.

steps.title: Check the exact Terraform state addresses
steps.instruction: From fa-terraform-beginner, run terraform state list and match all three addresses to this lab.
steps.description: Keep configuration and state available until cloud cleanup is complete.
steps.verification: Only the module VPC, subnet, and security-group addresses are listed.

steps.title: Create and review the destroy plan
steps.instruction: Run terraform plan -destroy -out=destroy.tfplan and inspect every proposed deletion.
steps.verification: Exactly three resources are proposed for destruction and no unrelated resource appears.

steps.title: Apply the reviewed destroy plan
steps.instruction: Run terraform apply destroy.tfplan only after the exact plan is confirmed.
steps.description: Allow Terraform to remove resources in dependency order.

steps.title: Verify state and AWS cleanup
steps.instruction: Run terraform state list and search VPC, Subnets, and Security groups for every recorded name and ID.
steps.verification: State is empty and all three lab resources are absent.

steps.title: Delete the local lab folder last
steps.instruction: Leave the folder, confirm its exact full path, and delete only fa-terraform-beginner.
steps.description: Remove local files only after the managed infrastructure is gone.
steps.verification: The lab folder is absent and unrelated local folders remain.

findings.message: Before candidate creation, confirm the currently installed Terraform and AWS provider versions and current AWS Console labels.

identityBinding.rule: A later separately approved write step must bind the currently signed-in Author and create a new draft identity.
